Quick answers at a glance:
- us-east-1 works for Hosted and Dedicated. Private (VPC) will require an infra runbook and a longer lead time (~6-8 weeks) if you want on-prem.
- For 60k tokens/month, Hosted with a reserved throughput lane is technically feasible but Dedicated gives predictable end-to-end latency SLOs and simpler auditability. Our recommendation: start Hosted reserved lane for the POC if time-to-value is highest priority, otherwise Dedicated if you need strict isolation.
- Differences: SLA specifics, log access cadence, and exportable audit bundles (Private > Dedicated > Hosted). I'll send a short doc summarizing the exact contractual changes.

Stephanie / Claire — quick tech notes from infra:

- us-east-1: fully supported across Hosted and Dedicated. We can pin a hosted-verified instance to that region; however, hosted customers are on shared control plane (data plane in us-east-1). If Acuity requires customer-controlled KMS or no shared metadata, Dedicated or Private is needed.
- Throughput: 60k tokens/month is light; if the pattern is bursty we recommend a small Dedicated pool (1-2 A100-equivalent cards) or a Hosted reserved lane with burst protection. Dedicated gives consistent tail latency.
- Networking: For Dedicated we'll provide static egress IPs for allowlist. For Private we need your VPC peer info and an SOW for the 6–8 week lead time.

I've attached a short cost sketch for Dedicated vs Hosted reserved lane (draft). If procurement prefers a TCO line-item I can formalize by EOD Wednesday.

Karthik

Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
